To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the wrench method is the most efficient, the "push" method is the most comfortable, and the "pull" method is the least comfortable.
the use of a wrench to operate a valve handwheel is a more effective way to open a valve than the use of a handwheel alone.
the use of a wrench to operate a handwheel valve can reduce the muscle activity in the upper extremity muscles and increase the muscle activity in trunk muscles compared with the handwheel alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a handwheel that will reduce the effort required to turn the wheel, and thus reduce the risk of injury.
the development of a more efficient and comfortable valve operation method.
the effects of different methods and torques on the muscle activity and comfort of operators of valve handwheels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method of valve handwheel operation is a very important factor in terms of the operator's comfort, safety, and efficiency.
the use of a torque wrench to operate a valve handwheel is the most efficient method for opening a valve, and is perceived by the operator as being the easiest to operate.
a wrench should be used when the torque requirement is above a certain value (in this study it was 50 Nm), and that the operator should be aware of the torque requirements of a valve.
